name: Morocco

findings.summary: Orange Maroc contracted Ericsson to modernise and expand its core network with a dual-mode, cloud-native 5G core ahead of a standalone 5G launch; no contract value was disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third pole. Scope is the core network; Orange Maroc's 5G RAN vendor was not established (Le360 also reports Nokia modernising Orange's network). Tier 3 on a named counterparty without value.

findings.local_actor: Maroc Telecom; Orange Maroc (reportedly also inwi)
findings.summary: Moroccan press reports Huawei already supplies Maroc Telecom and Orange Maroc, with Le360 saying over half of Moroccan telecom infrastructure reportedly runs on Huawei; no 5G equipment contract for the Maroc Telecom/inwi joint rollout was reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 3 as an existing supply relationship; the share claim is hedged ('reportedly') and unquantified by layer, so tier 5 was not coded. TelQuel (July 2025) says the Maroc Telecom/inwi consortium had not announced its 5G equipment winner. Only S3 sources, so not corroborated.

findings.controller: Nexus Core Systems-led consortium (with Naver Cloud, Nvidia, Lloyds Capital)
findings.local_actor: Maroc Telecom (go-to-market partner); TAQA Morocco (power); Casablanca-Settat region
findings.summary: A 500 MW AI data hub led by Nexus Core Systems, operated on Naver Cloud's platform with renewable power from TAQA Morocco, valued at US$1.2bn; sited at Nouaceur, permits obtained, design and procurement underway, first 40 MW phase delayed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: nationality of Nexus Core Systems and Lloyds Capital not stated in sources opened; Naver Cloud (Korean, third) operates the platform but ownership is unclear. Tier 2 because permits and procurement are reported but not construction or closed financing (works expected 2027-28 per BMI via Le360). The Q1 2026 phase-1 slip is a delay, not coded as a reversal. Nouaceur site attributed to Africa Intelligence via Hespress.

findings.local_actor: Nexus Core Systems / Naver Cloud AI hub
findings.summary: Nvidia is named as the GPU supplier for the planned Moroccan AI hub, with latest-generation Blackwell GB200 GPUs slated for the first 40 MW phase.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: GPU supply is stated as a plan; no purchase order, licence or delivery found. Only S3 sources opened mention Nvidia. US chip-export posture is covered by the global layer.

findings.summary: US startup Iozera announced a US$500m, 386 MW data centre and AI hub in Tetouan; a 2026 BMI-based report says commissioning is targeted for the second half of 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: an announcement made during a government roadshow; no contract, financing or construction start found in sources opened. Pole us from the owner's reported US domicile (North Africa Post); Le360 does not state nationality.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform
findings.summary: Morocco's digital transition minister told Reuters the country intends to build a 500 MW renewable-powered data centre in Dakhla; no developer, value or timeline was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no owner-operator named. Hespress links the Dakhla project to the Mistral MoU context (MAR-007), but no Mistral role in the facility is stated. Dakhla is in Western Sahara, whose status is disputed; coded under MAR as reported.

findings.local_actor: Ministry Delegate for Digital Transition and Administrative Reform
findings.summary: Morocco's digital transition minister and Mistral AI's CEO signed an MoU on AI skills, applied research, startup support, Moroccan-language work and better administrative services; no value disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Mistral is French, so third pole. Tier 1 (non-binding MoU). No deployment of Mistral models in Moroccan government found.

findings.summary: Per a 2020 Le360 fact-check, Huawei won one urban video-surveillance contract in Morocco, in Marrakech in 2015 as consortium lead; Casablanca's contracts went to non-Chinese firms and the DGSN does not procure city systems.
findings.analyst_inference: Pre-2020; still_current null. TelQuel (April 2025) says a newer Marrakech smart-camera project stalled and the city relies on the existing DGSN network, without naming its vendor. Le360's piece rebuts an Africa Intelligence claim of large-scale Huawei surveillance; contract value not given.

power.null_reason: TAQA Morocco renewable supply for the AI hub surfaced only as part of MAR-003; no dedicated AI power plant searched

research_gaps: Which vendor won the Maroc Telecom/inwi joint 5G equipment contract, and who supplies their RAN and core?
Is the 'over half of infrastructure on Huawei' claim documented by any S1/S2 source, by operator and layer?
Nexus Core Systems and Lloyds Capital: nationality and equity shares (sets MAR-003 facility pole); has construction or financing closed?
Iozera Tetouan: any binding agreement, financing or construction since 2024?
Dakhla 500 MW: developer, financing and any foreign partner.
April 2026 Huawei Maroc MoU with the judiciary council (MJCC) and July 2026 Vertiv MoU seen only in search titles; scope unknown.
Is the 2015 Huawei Marrakech surveillance system still in use; which vendors supply Rabat and Casablanca cameras (integrators named are Moroccan)?
Any Mistral or other frontier-model deployment in Moroccan government services; any Moroccan sovereign model?
